items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: I loved Bird when I finally heard Bird, and I didn’t find it all that radical when I heard him because I guess I’d been listening to stuff that, you know, post-bop, that was sort of in your head anyway.

ctx.x: So what was your passion as a young man.

My passion as a young man was always, like most kids I listened to the popular music of the day, I had my little transistor radio. Remember those little 9-volt transistor radios you used to put to your ear? Or you had the one earphone that stuck in. Yeah. So I had that and I generally listened to the black stations on the other end of the dial, you know, WWRL and I liked Motown and all that. But then my uncle, Lester Pelote, was a professional jazz guitarist in New York. He never really broke out of the local…

appearing on shows and he had the handkerchief and he didn’t play much trumpet at that point and I was just kind of wondering what’s so great about this guy. I mean everybody thinks he’s so wonderful. Because “Hello Dolly” was nice but I didn’t see it as anything that really knocked me out. So I went to the local library in Jersey City, the Fine Arts Library, and I pulled out an album that had an old track of Armstrong playing “Big Butter and Egg Man From the West” with the Hot Five. And I listened to it and…
